The logbook only re-aggregates the authors' released results.csv (not an independent classifier run), and the obtained values (68.929% and 33.671%) do not match the paper's claimed 68.4% and 38.3%, particularly for PartitionWise.

An independent synthetic experiment with X~U([-1,1]^8), Y~N(0,sigma(X_1)), 3000 calibration samples shows L1-ERT recovering 92% of the analytic violation (0.0866 vs 0.0948) at 30k test points while unaligned CovGap recovers only 5% (0.0049 vs 0.0948).

The same 30,000-point synthetic run estimates over-coverage at 0.0445 (analytic 0.0460) and under-coverage at 0.0464 (analytic 0.0488), both nonzero and close to theory, demonstrating the asymmetric decomposition.

The logbook only reads the official released classification CSV (80 rows) and checks internal consistency; it explicitly does not retrain image classifiers, so no independent experiment is performed to verify the reported divergent KL components.

A controlled experiment with 20 seeds, 2000 observations, and 5 folds shows a label memorizer produces false in-sample L2-ERT of 0.08886 but cross-fitted null ERT of 0, while a genuine two-region signal yields cross-fitted ERT of 0.01013, with zero train/evaluation overlap.

overall: The logbook provides independent numerical and synthetic-experiment evidence supporting claims 1, 3, 4, and 6, but for claims 2 and 5 it only re-aggregates the authors' released output files without independent model training, and the claim-2 numbers do not match the paper's reported values.
